record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one devise a register-program model based on elementary operations inspired by unitary quantum computation and use it to prove nontrivial consequences, for example for BQP?

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Devise a register program using basic instructions inspired by unitary computation, and use it to show non-trivial results for e.g. BQP.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A register program is a computational model in which a finite collection of registers (each holding a value from a specified domain, e.g., a bounded integer, a bit string, or an element of a field) is manipulated by a finite sequence of elementary instructions drawn from a fixed instruction set, possibly with control flow such as conditional branches and loops. The complexity class BQP is the class of decision problems solvable with bounded error in polynomial time on a quantum Turing machine using unitary quantum operations followed by a final measurement.\n\nDesign a register-program model whose basic instructions are inspired by the elementary operations of unitary quantum computation (for example, reversible/unitary updates such as conditional sign flips, controlled rotations on register entries, or amplitude-style linear combinations of register states), and which is rich enough to simulate or be related to BQP. Using this model, establish a nontrivial structural or complexity-theoretic consequence — for instance, a new upper bound, lower bound, simulation, or inclusion involving BQP or a related quantum complexity class — that goes beyond what is already known from standard quantum circuit or Turing-machine formulations.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a survey on space-efficient computation. No web evidence indicates a register-program model of the type described has been devised and used to derive nontrivial consequences for BQP; the problem appears to remain open.
